extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and parties interested in USPTO disciplinary actions
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order applying 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 to impose reciprocal discipline (exclusion) on a registrant for violations of professional-conduct rules, and setting related procedural and account-access conditions. Includes notice, limited recognition to close matters, publication, account restrictions, and reinstatement paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the exclusion is imposed for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) and is the appropriate reciprocal discipline where the registrant's state license was revoked by a duly constituted authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is predicated upon violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), i.e., being revoked from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the predicate was the Virginia State Bar Disciplinary Board's February 16, 2024 Order revoking Respondent's license after Respondent tendered Consent to Revocation while a disciplinary complaint, investigation, or proceeding was pending and acknowledged the material facts therein were true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline notice and opportunity to respond (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 providing the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order in this case was sent by certified mail; if delivery fails, the Notice may be published in the Official Gazette. The Notice must inform the respondent of the grounds in § 11.24(d)(1) on which to oppose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, Respondent did not file a response and the Office determined exclusion was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f) to conclude pending matters (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may be granted limited recognition pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f) for a specified short period (here, thirty (30) days) starting on the date of the Final Order so the respondent may endeavor to conclude work on behalf of clients on any matters pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such work cannot be concluded within the 30-day period, Respondent must advise each client so the client may make other arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Notice of Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the order's Notice of Exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice should identify the respondent, registration number, the fact of exclusion from practice before the USPTO, the regulatory basis (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), reference to the state disciplinary order, and where disciplinary decisions are available for public review (FOIA Reading Room URL).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO.gov account suspension/disablement upon expiration of limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective the date of the expiration of the 30-day limited recognition, the USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to Respondent (including all accounts the Respondent has ever established, sponsored, or used in connection with any trademark or patent matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority extends to disabling or suspending accounts; the order lists this as an immediate administrative consequence following the limited recognition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining/using/verifying/sponsoring USPTO.gov accounts until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a petition seeking reinstatement is granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, Respondent shall be prohibited from: (1) opening or activating any USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO; (2) applying for or attempting to apply for any USPTO.gov account(s); (3) verifying, or attempting to verify, any other person's credentials in connection with USPTO.gov account(s); and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated prohibitions prevent the respondent from re-entering electronic filing systems or facilitating others' access until formal reinstatement by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: No USPTO obligation to re-activate disabled accounts; respondent must initiate re-activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the order obligates the USPTO to take action sua sponte to re-activate any USPTO.gov account disabled or suspended pursuant to the order; it is Respondent's sole responsibility to initiate any such re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that administrative reactivation is not automatic and places burden on respondent to seek re-activation after satisfying reinstatement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure governed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition seeking reinstatement to practice before the USPTO must be filed and granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 for the respondent to be restored to practice and regain the ability to hold or use USPTO.gov accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly conditions many prohibitions and account restrictions on the respondent remaining unreinstated until § 11.60 relief is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service requirements for disciplinary orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be served on the respondent by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.1 l(a), and to addresses where the OED Director reasonably believes the respondent receives mail; copies may be sent to counsel via e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes an explicit Certificate of Service section showing method of service and addresses used (physical address and counsel email), which evidences compliance with service protocols.
